caption:
A pattern-of-life baseline is not instant. It takes repeated passes over a site before the system can tell you what's normal there — and only once normal is established does an anomaly mean anything.

On a new site, week one gives you an image. Week six gives you a baseline. Flagging deviation before that baseline exists is guesswork dressed as intelligence.

This is why standing tasking on a new area of interest starts quiet by design. The capability isn't slow to react — it's refusing to call a false alarm real just to look responsive on day one.
thread: A pattern-of-life baseline takes time to build. Anomaly detection means nothing until normal is established first.
New site, week one: an image. Week six: a baseline. Flag deviation before that baseline exists and you're guessing, not assessing.
Standing tasking on a new area of interest starts quiet on purpose. That's the baseline forming, not a coverage gap.
Confidence in a flag is only as good as the history behind it. No history, no confidence — regardless of the alert.

card.headline: No baseline, no anomaly
card.sub: Pattern of life takes repeated passes to establish. Deviation only means something once normal is known.

rationale: Fills a real capability gap not yet covered — the baseline-building limit — while reinforcing the confirmed/assessed/unknown discipline without repeating prior phrasing.
